options.description: The agent turns judge questions into plain questions in your terms and merges the ones that hinge on one principle. When one looks obvious, it sends it back to the judge with its reason, and the judge withdraws it or keeps it. The agent never drops one on its own, so the independence stays.
options.label: Rephrase, merge, push back (Recommended)

options.description: The agent drops a question it finds obvious or irrelevant and logs why, and you can read the log. Fewer questions and faster, but the agent that wrote the record then partly judges its own work.
options.label: Agent may drop obvious ones

options.description: No agent in between. The judge itself gets stricter about relevance and about what your records already answer before it asks.
options.label: Judge asks, better filtered

payload.question: When the judge raises a question about a record, the coding agent would receive it and put its own question to you. Today the judge is kept independent of the agent that wrote the record, so the agent never decides for you. How far may the agent go with a judge's question?
